relations.what: the first check_ptr call creates and returns the shadow pointer head_s
head_s records the pseudo-pointer's base value at allocation time
head_s points to the real memory base address of the provisioned object
the second check_ptr call looks up head_s to translate curr_v into a real pointer
combining curr_v with head_s's recorded bases yields the real pointer and its dereferenced value

steps.what: the first check_ptr invocation creates the shadow pointer, records the pseudo-pointer base, and allocates Obj 1 from Seed 2
steps.carries: head (pseudo-pointer, head=1) and the newly allocated Obj 1

steps.what: the second check_ptr invocation leverages the recorded shadow-pointer data to return the translated real pointer curr_v - pseudo_ptr_base + real_ptr_base
steps.carries: curr_v (pseudo-pointer offset, curr_v=-3) and the resulting real pointer p_v = 0xfefc

content.key_idea: A shadow pointer created by the first check_ptr call remembers an object's pseudo- and real-address bases; a later check_ptr call reuses that record to translate a new pseudo-pointer offset into the correct real memory address.
content.reading_order: Follow the downward code-flow arrow through step ① into head_s and the memory table, then into the second code box and back to head_s at step ②.

summary: Figure 5 traces how UCSAN's shadow-pointer mechanism creates and later translates a pointer to Obj 1 allocated from Seed 2. A bold code-flow arrow leads from a first code snippet, where check_ptr(head, head_s) both allocates the object and creates its shadow pointer head_s, recording a pseudo-pointer base of 0x01 and a real-pointer base of 0xff00 that points into the 'Provisioned Obj 1 In Memory' table. Step (1) marks this creation. Later, a second code snippet computes a new pseudo-pointer offset (curr_v = -3) and calls check_ptr(curr_v, head_s) again; step (2) marks how this second call reuses head_s's recorded bases to compute the real pointer curr_v - pseudo_ptr_base + real_ptr_base, yielding p_v = 0xfefc and dereferencing the value 0x65. A shared Legends box defines the Seed, Phantom Seed, Control Flow, and Obj point-to symbols used across the paper's figures.
